q: 分布式 Rate Limiter 的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are core functional requirements for a distributed rate limiter? (multi-select)
options: 长期保存所有限流日志用于复杂分析
按 user ID、IP 或 API key 识别 client
基于可配置规则限制 HTTP 请求
超限时返回 HTTP 429 并带有有用 headers
why: 限流器要按身份识别 client、按可配置规则限速、超限返回带 headers 的 429；复杂查询和长期日志分析都不在范围内。
why_en: The rate limiter must identify clients, enforce configurable request rules, and return a helpful 429 when a client exceeds its quota.
options_en: Persist all rate-limit logs long term for analytics
Identify clients by user ID, IP, or API key
Enforce configurable rules on HTTP requests
Return HTTP 429 with useful headers when exceeded

termDefinitions.meaning: 开发者调用 API 时使用的密钥标识，用来区分调用方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a credential that identifies which developer or app is calling the API.

termDefinitions.meaning: Too Many Requests 的标准状态码，用于超限拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 429 is the standard status code for Too Many Requests.

optionExplanations: 这属于事后分析能力，不是本题要保证的实时限流功能，加进来会让核心路径背上存储和查询包袱。
这是限流器工作的前提——不先分清是谁在发请求，就没法把额度记到正确的桶里。
规则要能配、不能写死在代码里，否则每次调整限额都要重新发布。
只拒绝还不够，客户端要知道还剩多少配额、什么时候能重试，否则只会继续硬打。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping every rate-limit log around long term is an after-the-fact analytics capability, not something the real-time limiter itself needs to guarantee, and it saddles the hot path with extra storage and query burden.
This is the starting assumption the limiter runs on — without first telling who's making the request, there's no correct bucket to charge it to.
Rules need to stay configurable rather than hard-coded, or every limit change would require a new deploy.
Rejecting alone isn't enough — the client needs to know how much quota is left and when it can try again, or it just keeps hammering the API.

q: 本题的核心非功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are the core non-functional requirements for this design? (multi-select)
options: 每次检查引入的额外延迟小于约 10ms
跨所有节点提供强一致限流保证
高可用，允许节点间限流状态短暂最终一致
支撑约 1M requests/sec 和 100M DAU
why: 限流检查必须快且可用：延迟目标小于 10ms，允许最终一致，同时要撑住约 1M requests/sec、100M DAU 的量级；强一致的跨节点保证不在范围内。
why_en: The limiter must add under 10ms of latency, stay highly available with eventual consistency, and handle roughly one million requests per second across 100 million daily users.
options_en: Extra latency per check under about 10ms
Strongly consistent limits across every node
High availability with brief cross-node eventual consistency
Support roughly 1M requests/sec and 100M DAU
optionExplanations: 每次检查最多加 10ms 延迟，这样限流检查才不会成为请求路径上的新瓶颈。
要求所有节点严格同步意味着每次判断都要跨节点协调，这和限流要低延迟、高可用的目标正好相反。
允许限流状态短暂最终一致换来的是高可用——个别节点稍微看到旧值也没关系，好过为了强一致牺牲可用性。
百万级请求量、上亿日活这个规模，决定了后面必须做分布式分片，而不是单机就能扛住。
optionExplanations_en: Capping added latency at under 10ms keeps the check from becoming a new bottleneck on the request path.
Requiring every node to stay strictly in sync means coordinating across nodes on every check, which fights directly against the low-latency, high-availability goal.
Accepting brief eventual consistency buys high availability — a node seeing a slightly stale value is fine, better than sacrificing uptime for strict sync.
A rough one-million-requests-per-second, hundred-million-DAU scale is exactly what forces the design into distributed sharding instead of a single machine.

scenario: 面试官确认设计目标：约 1M requests/sec 的流量，覆盖 100M 日活用户的社交平台 API。
scenario_en: The interviewer confirms the target: about 1M requests/sec across a social platform API with 100M daily active users.
q: 这个规模对限流器的实现方式排除了什么？
q_en: What does this scale rule out for how the rate limiter is implemented?
options: 单机本地计数或单个 Redis 实例保存全部限流状态
把限流放在 API Gateway 边缘层做
使用 Token Bucket 算法
允许限流状态跨节点最终一致
why: 1M rps/100M DAU 排除的是单点状态：无论是单机 in-process 计数还是单个 Redis 实例，都撑不住这个吞吐和多实例场景，必须做成分布式分片。
why_en: At roughly one million requests per second, a single in-process counter or single Redis instance cannot hold all the state, so the design must shard.
options_en: A single in-process counter or single Redis instance holding all state
Placing the limiter at the API Gateway edge layer
Using the Token Bucket algorithm
Letting rate-limit state be eventually consistent across nodes
optionExplanations: 1M rps 这个量级下，无论是单机内存计数还是单个 Redis 实例，吞吐和内存都撑不住，这正是被排除的实现方式。
把限流放在网关是部署位置的选择，跟这道题问的「单点状态撑不住」没有直接关系。
选哪种算法是另一个维度的决定，规模大小本身不排斥 Token Bucket。
允许状态最终一致恰恰是应对这个规模常用的手段，不是被这个规模排除掉的东西。
optionExplanations_en: At roughly 1M rps, neither an in-process counter nor a single Redis instance has the throughput or memory to hold all the state — that's precisely what gets ruled out.
Where the limiter sits is a placement decision, not directly what this question about a single point of state being unable to keep up is asking.
Which algorithm to use is a separate axis of the design; scale alone doesn't rule out Token Bucket.
Accepting eventually consistent state is actually a common tool for handling this scale, not something the scale rules out.

q: 补全限流器的三个核心实体：
q_en: Fill in the rate limiter's three core entities:
text: 核心实体是 {{Rules}}（限流策略）、{{Clients}}（被限制的用户/IP/API key）、{{Requests}}（携带 endpoint、身份、timestamp 的待判断请求）。
why: 三实体协作做一次 allow/deny：Request 带 endpoint(选哪条 Rule)、身份(找哪个 Client 的计数)、timestamp(定位哪个时间窗)。判断=这个 Client 在这个窗口内对这个 endpoint 的请求数 < Rule 上限就放行、否则拒。缺任一字段都判不了。
why_en: The three entities cooperate for one allow/deny decision: a Request carries endpoint (which Rule applies), identity (which Client's counter), and timestamp (which time window). Decision = if this Client's count for this endpoint in this window is below the Rule's limit, allow, else deny. Miss any field and you cannot decide.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流策略，定义在什么维度、什么时间窗口内允许多少请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rules define how many requests are allowed for a given scope and time window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被限流的对象，比如某个用户、IP 或 API key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clients are the entities being rate limited, such as a user, IP, or API key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 待判断的请求，带三个决策必需字段：endpoint(用来选哪条 Rule)、身份(找哪个 Client 的计数)、timestamp(定位哪个时间窗)——缺一个就没法判 allow/deny
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A request to be judged, carrying the three fields the decision needs: endpoint (which Rule), identity (which Client counter), and timestamp (which time window).

termDefinitions.term: 按请求计数·按 endpoint 定额
termDefinitions.meaning: 限流按每个 HTTP 请求计数(不是按页面)。「60 请求/分钟」这类正常浏览没事，因为限额是按 endpoint 校准的——便宜接口(浏览/feed)高限额或不限；敏感接口(登录/提交)低限额(如 5/分=防暴力)。静态资源多走 CDN、不计入。这正是 Rule 带 endpoint 字段的意义
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Limits count per HTTP request (not per page). Normal browsing at ~60/min is fine because limits are calibrated per endpoint — cheap endpoints get high/no limits; sensitive ones (login/submit) get low limits to stop abuse; static assets go via CDN uncounted. This is why a Rule carries the endpoint.

rows: 找该 Client 的计数器

codeSample:
Rule：/login → 每分钟每客户端 5 次

Request：{ endpoint:/login, 身份:apikey_ABC, timestamp:10:00:30 }
  ① endpoint=/login    → 找到 Rule（5 次/分钟）
  ② 身份=apikey_ABC    → 找到该 Client 的计数器
  ③ timestamp=10:00:30 → 落在窗口 10:00:00–10:01:00
  ④ 窗口内已用 4 < 5    → 放行，计数 →5
下一个同窗口请求 → 5 ≥ 5 → 拒绝(429)

scenario: 应用或网关需要调用限流组件，既要知道是否通过，也要能生成响应 headers。
scenario_en: An app or gateway calls the rate-limit component and needs both the allow/deny result and enough data to build response headers.
q: 最合适的限流接口返回形态是什么？
q_en: What should the rate-limit interface return?
options: getAllTrafficLogs(startTime, endTime) -> Log[]
isRequestAllowed(clientId, ruleId) -> { passes, remaining, resetTime }
setUserPassword(userId, newPassword) -> boolean
renderTimeline(userId, page, pageSize) -> Post[]
why: 接口按「调用方拿它干嘛」设计：网关既要判放行、又要生成限流响应头。所以返回 3 个——passes(放行否)、remaining(剩余额度→X-RateLimit-Remaining 头)、resetTime(窗口重置→X-RateLimit-Reset/Retry-After 头)。其余选项是别的领域的函数，跟限流判断无关。
why_en: Design the interface around what the caller does with it: a gateway must both decide pass/block and emit rate-limit headers. So it returns three things — passes (allow?), remaining (quota left → X-RateLimit-Remaining), and resetTime (window reset → X-RateLimit-Reset/Retry-After). The other options are functions from unrelated domains.
whenOtherWins: 只有离线分析系统才需要批量日志查询接口；在线限流路径必须保持极简低延迟。
tradeoff: 极简判断接口 vs 支持复杂查询/分析
options_en: getAllTrafficLogs(startTime, endTime) -> Log[]
isRequestAllowed(clientId, ruleId) -> { passes, remaining, resetTime }
setUserPassword(userId, newPassword) -> boolean
renderTimeline(userId, page, pageSize) -> Post[]
optionExplanations: 批量拉日志是离线分析接口，回答不了单次请求该不该放行这个在线问题。
passes 直接给出放行/拒绝，remaining 和 resetTime 正好对应 429 响应要用到的 headers 字段。
改密码是账户管理操作，跟限流判断完全是两码事。
渲染时间线是内容展示逻辑，跟这次请求该不该被限流毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Fetching a batch of logs is an offline-analytics interface — it doesn't answer whether this single request should be allowed right now.
passes gives the allow/deny call directly, and remaining plus resetTime map straight onto the fields a 429 response needs.
Changing a password is an account-management action, unrelated to a rate-limit decision.
Rendering a timeline is content-display logic, with nothing to do with whether this request should be throttled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标准限流响应头：Limit(上限)、Remaining(剩余)、Reset(重置时间)；被拒时再配 Retry-After。接口返回 remaining/resetTime 正是为了填这些头
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Standard rate-limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset (plus Retry-After when blocked); the interface returns remaining/resetTime to fill them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超出限额时返回的 HTTP 状态码，通常带 Retry-After 告诉客户端多久后可重试
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 429 is returned when the limit is exceeded, usually with a Retry-After telling the client when to retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两者都说「你何时能再请求」：X-RateLimit-Reset 是「绝对时刻」(窗口重置的时间戳，如 10:01:00)；Retry-After 是「还要等多久」(相对秒数，如 30s)。关系：Retry-After = resetTime − now。Retry-After 更好用(睡 N 秒就重试、不用对时)，随 429 一起发
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Both say when you can request again: X-RateLimit-Reset is an absolute moment (the window-reset timestamp); Retry-After is a relative delay in seconds. Retry-After = resetTime − now, and it is the easy-to-act-on value sent with a 429.

scenario: 每个应用服务器在本地内存里维护计数，无网络调用，速度极快；但请求经负载均衡分散到多台服务器。
scenario_en: Each app server keeps counts in local memory with no network calls, so it's very fast — but the load balancer spreads requests across many servers.
q: 这种 in-process rate limiter 的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with this in-process rate limiter?
options: 它一定比 Redis 慢
它无法识别请求里的 IP
每台服务器只看到本机流量，无法精确执行全局限额
它会自动产生跨实例强一致
why: 5 台服务器各自计数时，每台都可能觉得没超限，但全局请求量早已超标；in-process 只适合单实例或能接受近似误差的场景。
why_en: An in-process limiter looks fast, but each server only sees its own traffic, so a client can multiply its real limit by the number of servers.
whenOtherWins: 单应用实例、小流量服务，或能接受按服务器数近似放大限额时，in-process 依然简单有效。
tradeoff: 本地零网络跳的速度 vs 跨实例的全局精确限额
options_en: It is always slower than Redis
It cannot read the IP address from a request
Each server only sees its own traffic, so global limits become approximate
It automatically gives strong cross-instance consistency

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流状态保存在应用进程内存里，不跨实例共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process rate limiter keeps counters in local memory that is not shared across instances.

optionExplanations: in-process 恰恰是最快的——没有网络跳；问题不是速度，是看不到全局。
本地进程照样能读到请求里的 IP，识别能力本身没问题，问题出在状态不共享。
5 台服务器各自计数，每台都可能觉得自己没超限，但全局早就超了，这才是它的真正问题。
in-process 各算各的，说反了——它天生就没有跨实例一致性，更别提强一致。
optionExplanations_en: In-process is actually the fastest option — no network hop; the problem isn't speed, it's the lack of a global view.
A local process can still read the IP from a request just fine — the issue isn't identification, it's unshared state.
Five servers each counting on their own can all think they're under the limit while the real global total is already over it — that's the actual problem.
In-process instances each count independently — this has it backwards, since it has no cross-instance consistency at all, let alone a strong one.

scenario: 应用需要传入 subscription tier、账户状态、endpoint 等丰富上下文，并希望限流逻辑独立部署。
scenario_en: The app needs to pass rich context like subscription tier, account status, and endpoint, and wants the rate-limiting logic deployed independently.
q: 哪种部署形态最灵活？
q_en: Which deployment shape is most flexible?
options: 每个客户端本地各自限流
只用 CDN 缓存
把限流写进数据库触发器
专用 Rate Limiting Service
why: 专用服务能维护全局精确状态，还能吃到应用层丰富上下文（订阅等级、账号状态）做复杂规则；代价是多一次网络往返和一个新的故障点。
why_en: A dedicated rate-limiting service gives global precision and rich application context, at the cost of an extra network hop and a new failure point.
whenOtherWins: 只需要边缘 HTTP 级限流时，API Gateway 集成更常见，且少一次到限流服务的调用。
tradeoff: 丰富业务上下文与全局精确 vs 额外网络跳和故障点
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Gateway[API Gateway]
Gateway --> Limiter[Rate Limiter]
Limiter --> Redis[(Redis)]
Gateway --> App[Backend API]
options_en: Each client rate-limits itself locally
Rely on CDN caching alone
Implement limiting inside a database trigger
A dedicated rate-limiting service
optionExplanations: 把限流丢给每个客户端自己执行，虽然部署简单，但完全看不到全局状态，也管不了不听话的客户端。
CDN 缓存能顶掉重复的静态内容请求，但它不理解每个用户的订阅等级、账号状态这类业务上下文，做不了细粒度限流判断。
把限流逻辑塞进数据库触发器，意味着每次判断都要绕到数据库这一层，既慢又难独立部署和扩展。
拆成一个独立的限流服务，能吃到应用传来的订阅等级、账号状态等丰富上下文，还能单独部署扩容，代价是多一次网络跳。
optionExplanations_en: Handing limiting entirely to each client is simple to deploy, but it has no view of global state and can't stop a client that ignores it.
CDN caching absorbs repeated static content requests, but it doesn't understand a user's subscription tier or account status, so it can't make fine-grained limiting decisions.
Putting limiting logic inside a database trigger routes every decision through the database layer, which is slow and hard to deploy or scale on its own.

Splitting limiting into its own service lets it take rich context like subscription tier and account status from the app, and it can be deployed and scaled independently — at the cost of one more network hop.

scenario: 目标是保护后端服务，让被拒请求尽早挡在入口；限流依据主要来自 HTTP header、路径、IP 和 JWT。
scenario_en: The goal is to protect backend services by rejecting bad requests as early as possible; limiting decisions rely mainly on HTTP headers, path, IP, and the JWT.
q: 该设计最终选择的限流部署位置是什么？
q_en: Where does this design finally place the rate limiter?
options: API Gateway 边缘层直接拒绝
每个业务 handler 内部单独判断
用户本地客户端
离线数据仓库
why: 网关限流能在请求进入应用前直接返回 429，是生产系统最常见的做法；限制是只能看到 HTTP 请求本身的信息，深层业务上下文要编码进 JWT 等载体。
why_en: Gateway-level rate limiting rejects abusive traffic before it reaches backend services, though it only sees what is visible in the HTTP request itself.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则依赖大量应用内部状态（比如实时账户余额），专用服务或应用内检查会更合适。
tradeoff: 边缘早拒绝、零额外跳 vs 只看到请求本身、看不到深层业务状态
options_en: The API Gateway rejects at the edge
Each business handler checks individually
The user's local client
An offline data warehouse

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把身份声明编码进 token 的格式，网关可以直接读取而不用查库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT encodes identity claims into a token that a gateway can read without a database call.

optionExplanations: 网关能在请求碰到任何业务代码之前就直接拒绝，是保护后端最早的一道关口；代价是只能看到 HTTP 请求本身能提供的信息。
把判断散落到每个业务 handler 里，意味着请求已经真正进了应用、消耗了资源之后才被拒绝，保护不到后端。
限流逻辑放在用户自己的客户端，用户可以随时绕过或篡改，起不到真正的强制作用。
数据仓库是事后分析用的，等结果算出来时超限请求早就打进后端了，来不及拦。
optionExplanations_en: The gateway rejects a request before it ever touches business code, the earliest possible protection point; the tradeoff is it only sees what's visible in the HTTP request itself.
Scattering the check across every business handler means a request has already entered the app and consumed resources before getting rejected — too late to protect the backend.
Putting the logic in the user's own client leaves it free to bypass or tamper with it — no real enforcement.
A data warehouse is for after-the-fact analysis; by the time it computes anything, the over-limit request has already hit the backend.

q: API Gateway 可用于识别 client 的常见标识有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which identifiers can an API Gateway use to identify a client? (multi-select)
options: JWT / Authorization header 中的 userId
X-Forwarded-For 中的 IP address
查数据库拿用户订阅等级（每次请求都额外查一次）
X-API-Key 中的 API key
why: 网关主要靠请求本身可见的信息识别 client；额外查库这类网络调用会拖慢每个请求，除非把结果提前编码进 JWT claim 带到边缘。
why_en: A gateway limiter typically identifies clients from information already in the request, such as a JWT claim, forwarded IP, or API key header, instead of an extra database call.
options_en: The userId inside a JWT / Authorization header
The IP address inside X-Forwarded-For
Query a database for subscription tier on every request
The API key inside X-API-Key

termDefinitions.meaning: 把身份信息编码进 token 的格式，常放在 Authorization header。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a token format that encodes identity claims, usually sent in the Authorization header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录请求经过的代理链路上真实客户端 IP 的 HTTP header。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: X-Forwarded-For is an HTTP header that carries the original client IP through a chain of proxies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开发者调用 API 时使用的密钥标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a credential that identifies which developer or app is calling the API.

optionExplanations: JWT 是请求自带的信息，网关解出 userId 不用额外查库，符合本题不能拖慢每个请求的约束。
IP 同样是请求本身携带的字段，网关直接读 header 就能拿到，不产生额外网络调用。
每个请求都去查一次数据库拿订阅等级，等于给网关限流路径加了一次额外网络往返，跟低延迟目标冲突。
X-API-Key 同样在请求头里直接可读，跟 JWT、IP 一样不需要额外查询。
optionExplanations_en: A JWT already travels with the request, so the gateway can read the userId without an extra database call.
The IP address is also carried in the request itself, so the gateway reads it straight from the header with no extra network hop.
Looking up subscription tier in a database on every request adds a network round trip to the gateway's hot path, which fights the low-latency goal.
The API key is likewise readable straight from a request header, no extra lookup needed, same as the JWT and IP.

q: 真实系统通常会叠加哪些限流规则？（多选）
q_en: Which rate-limit rules do real systems typically layer together? (multi-select)
options: per-user limit
per-IP limit
global API capacity limit
endpoint-specific limit
why: 真实系统很少只有一个全局数字：per-user、per-IP、全局容量、endpoint 级规则会同时生效，命中最严格的一条就拒绝。
why_en: Production systems layer per-user, per-IP, global, and endpoint-specific limits, and enforce whichever rule is hit first.
options_en: A per-user limit
A per-IP limit
A global API capacity limit
An endpoint-specific limit
optionExplanations: per-user limit 挡住单个账号把配额刷爆的情况，是最贴身的一层。
per-IP limit 补上未登录或跨账号但同源的流量，防止绕开 user 维度的滥用。
global API capacity limit 是最后一道闸门，防止再多规则叠加也压不住的整体过载。
endpoint-specific limit 让重的接口（比如搜索、上传）单独收紧，不被轻接口的宽松额度带偏。
optionExplanations_en: A per-user limit stops a single account from burning through its own quota — the most personal layer.
A per-IP limit catches traffic that isn't logged in, or spread across accounts from one source, closing gaps the user-level rule misses.
A global API capacity limit is the last gate, protecting the whole system when every other rule combined still isn't enough.
An endpoint-specific limit lets a heavy endpoint like search or upload get tighter caps without being dragged along by a lighter endpoint's generous quota.

scenario: 多个真实用户可能共享同一个出口 IP（公司网络、公共 WiFi），但都已登录拿到各自账号。
scenario_en: Multiple real users can share the same egress IP (corporate network, public WiFi), but they are all logged in with their own accounts.
q: User ID 限流相比 IP 限流的主要优势是什么？
q_en: What is the main advantage of user-ID limiting over IP limiting?
options: IP 限流更精确，因为公网 IP 从不重复分配
已登录场景更公平：不会把共享 IP 下的多个用户误判成一个
User ID 限流不需要用户先登录鉴权
两者对完全匿名流量的效果完全一样
why: IP 天然适合匿名流量，但 NAT、公共 WiFi 会把很多真实用户并成一个 IP；已登录场景优先按 userId 分配限额更公平。
why_en: User-ID limits are fairer for logged-in traffic because IP limits can lump many real users behind the same NAT or public network into one bucket.
tradeoff: 已登录场景的公平性 vs 匿名流量下的可用性
options_en: IP limiting is more precise because public IPs are never reused
It is fairer for logged-in users because a shared IP will not be mistaken for one user
User-ID limiting does not require the user to log in first
Both behave identically for fully anonymous traffic

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个设备共用同一个公网 IP 出口的网络地址转换机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAT lets many devices share one public IP address when talking to the internet.

optionExplanations: 公网 IP 其实经常被复用和轮换（运营商 NAT、动态分配），把它当成永久唯一标识本身就不成立。
已登录场景下按 userId 分配额度，公司网络或公共 WiFi 下的多个真实用户不会被误判成同一个人在刷请求。
userId 限流恰恰依赖用户已经登录、系统知道是谁，这个选项说反了。
匿名流量根本没有 userId 可用，这时候只能退回 IP 限流，两者并不是等价的。
optionExplanations_en: Public IPs are frequently reused or rotated by carriers and NAT, so treating one as a permanent unique identity doesn't hold up.
For logged-in traffic, limiting by userId means several real people behind a shared office or public WiFi network won't get mistaken for one abuser.
User-ID limiting actually depends on the user already being logged in and identified — this option has it backwards.
Anonymous traffic has no userId to key off of, so IP limiting is the fallback there — the two aren't interchangeable.

q: Fixed Window Counter 的主要缺陷是什么？
q_en: What is the main flaw of the Fixed Window Counter algorithm?
options: 必须为每个请求单独存 timestamp
完全无法实现请求计数
窗口边界处可能双倍突发（两个相邻窗口各打满一次）
永远不能返回 reset time
why: 固定窗口简单省内存，但窗口切换瞬间没有平滑：用户可以在旧窗口尾部和新窗口头部各打满一次，短时间内拿到两倍配额。
why_en: Fixed windows are simple, but a client can burst up to twice its limit right across a window boundary.
tradeoff: 实现极简、只存一个计数器 vs 窗口边界处的突发失控
options_en: It must store a separate timestamp for every request
It cannot implement request counting at all
Two adjacent windows can each be maxed out, doubling the effective burst
It can never return a reset time
optionExplanations: 固定窗口恰恰不需要单独存每个请求的 timestamp，一个计数器就够了，这个说法说反了。
固定窗口本身就是靠计数实现的，说它完全不能计数是自相矛盾。
窗口切换那一刻没有平滑处理，client 可以在旧窗口尾部和新窗口头部各打满一次，短时间内拿到两倍配额。
窗口边界本身就是确定的时间点，固定窗口反而很容易算出 reset time。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed window actually doesn't need a per-request timestamp at all — one counter is enough, so this has it backwards.
Fixed window is literally built around counting requests, so saying it can't count at all is self-contradictory.
The window switch itself isn't smoothed, so a client can max out the tail of the old window and the head of the new one, getting double its quota in a short burst.
Window boundaries are fixed, known points in time, so fixed window is actually one of the easier algorithms to compute a reset time from.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["窗口1 末尾 10:00:59
打满 5 个 ✅ count=5"] --> B["边界 10:01:00
count 重置为 0"] B --> C["窗口2 开头 10:01:01
再打满 5 个 ✅ count=5"] C --> D["⚠️ 边界前后 ~2 秒内共 10 个
= 2× 突发"]

q: Sliding Window Log 的优点和代价是什么？
q_en: What are the benefit and cost of the Sliding Window Log algorithm?
options: 只需两个整数，但很不准确
支持突发流量，但不限制长期速率
完全不需要存储任何状态
精确统计滑动窗口请求，但要存大量 timestamp
why: 日志法记录每次请求时间，能精确回答过去 N 分钟发生了多少次，没有固定窗口的边界问题；代价是每个热点 client 要存、清理大量 timestamp。
why_en: Sliding window logs are exact because they track every request timestamp, but that precision costs memory and cleanup work per client.
tradeoff: 精确无边界效应 vs 每个 client 的存储与扫描开销
options_en: Only needs two integers, but is very inaccurate
Allows bursts, but does not cap sustained rate
Needs no stored state at all
Exact per-request count, but stores many timestamps
optionExplanations: 只用两个整数是 Sliding Window Counter 的做法，Sliding Window Log 反而要为每个请求单独存 timestamp。
它对每个滑动窗口内的请求数是精确统计的，长期速率同样被这个窗口卡住，这个说法不成立。
它恰恰需要为每个 client 存一长串 timestamp，是这四个算法里状态最重的一个。
记录每次请求的精确时间，回答过去 N 分钟发生了多少次不会有偏差，代价是热点 client 要存和清理大量 timestamp。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping just two integers is the Sliding Window Counter's trick — Sliding Window Log instead stores a separate timestamp for every single request.
It counts requests inside a sliding window exactly, and that same window caps the sustained rate too, so this claim doesn't hold.
It actually needs a long list of stored timestamps per client — the heaviest state footprint of the four algorithms.
Recording every request's exact timestamp answers how many happened in the last N minutes with no bias, at the cost of storing and cleaning a lot of timestamps for a hot client.

q: Sliding Window Counter 如何在成本和准确性之间折中？
q_en: How does the Sliding Window Counter trade off cost against accuracy?
options: 维护当前窗口和上一窗口两个计数器，按时间进度加权估算
保存所有请求的精确 timestamp
完全忽略上一窗口的数据
让 Redis 每秒重启清空状态
why: 它用当前窗口和上一窗口两个计数器，按当前窗口已过去的比例加权估算真实滑动窗口值，比固定窗口准，比日志省内存。
why_en: Sliding window counters approximate a true sliding window by weighting the previous and current window counters.
tradeoff: 内存只要两个计数器 vs 假设流量在窗口内均匀分布的近似误差
options_en: Keep current and previous window counters, weighted by elapsed time
Store the exact timestamp of every request
Ignore the previous window entirely
Restart Redis every second to clear state
optionExplanations: 只维护当前和上一窗口两个计数器，按当前窗口已过去的比例加权估算，比日志省内存、比固定窗口准。
存精确 timestamp 是 Sliding Window Log 的做法，跟这里只用两个计数器的思路正好相反。
完全不看上一窗口就退化成了 Fixed Window，滑动窗口计数器的关键恰恰是要用上一窗口做加权。
每秒清空状态等于每次都从零开始算，跟「维护两个计数器估算滑动值」这个思路完全不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping just the current and previous window counters, weighted by how far the current window has progressed, is cheaper than a full log and more accurate than a fixed window.
Storing exact timestamps for every request is what Sliding Window Log does — the opposite of using just two counters here.
Ignoring the previous window entirely collapses this back into Fixed Window; the whole point of the sliding counter is weighting in that previous window.
Wiping state every second just restarts the count from zero each time, which isn't the same idea as weighting two counters to estimate a sliding value.

scenario: API 流量天然 bursty，需要允许短暂突发，但也要限制长期平均速率，并且每个 client 状态要很小。
scenario_en: API traffic is naturally bursty: short bursts must be allowed, long-term average rate must still be capped, and per-client state must stay small.
q: 该设计最终选择哪种限流算法？
q_en: Which rate-limiting algorithm does this design finally choose?
options: 完整 Sliding Window Log
Token Bucket
全局互斥锁
只用 fixed window
why: Token Bucket 用 bucket capacity 控制突发、refill rate 控制长期速率，每个 client 只需两个字段，省内存又贴合 bursty 流量。
why_en: Token Bucket balances burst tolerance and sustained-rate control while needing only two small fields per client.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须精确限制任意滚动窗口内的请求数，Sliding Window Log 更准；规模很小时 Fixed Window 也够用。
tradeoff: 突发容忍加小状态 vs 任意滚动窗口的精确计数
options_en: A full Sliding Window Log
Token Bucket
A global mutex lock
Fixed window only
optionExplanations: 完整日志能精确统计滑动窗口内的请求数，但要为每个热点 client 存大量 timestamp，跟这里要求的小状态相冲突。
bucket capacity 管住突发上限，refill rate 管住长期平均速率，每个 client 只要两个字段，同时满足突发容忍和小状态。
全局锁会让所有 client 的请求排成一队等同一把锁，直接杀死并发，跟高吞吐目标背道而驰。
fixed window 只有一个计数器确实省内存，但窗口边界处会出现双倍突发，没法真正卡住长期速率。
optionExplanations_en: A full log counts a sliding window exactly, but storing every timestamp for a hot client fights the small-per-client-state requirement here.
Bucket capacity caps the burst and refill rate caps the sustained average, needing only two fields per client — burst tolerance and small state together.
A global mutex lock forces every client's requests to queue behind one lock, killing concurrency and working against the high-throughput target.
Fixed window is cheap with a single counter, but it can double-burst right across a window boundary, so it doesn't actually cap the sustained rate.

q: 补全 Token Bucket 的两个核心参数：
q_en: Fill in Token Bucket's two core parameters:
text: Token Bucket 用 {{bucket capacity}} 控制最大突发，用 {{refill rate}} 控制长期平均请求速率；每次请求消耗一个 token。
why: capacity 回答“最多能一口气打多少”，refill rate 回答“长期平均允许多少”；这比单纯请求数窗口更贴近 bursty 的 API 流量。
why_en: Token Bucket uses bucket capacity for burst size and refill rate for sustained request rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: token bucket 能装下的最大 token 数，决定允许的突发上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bucket capacity is the maximum number of tokens a bucket can hold, which caps how large a burst can be.

termDefinitions.meaning: token 补充进 bucket 的速率，决定长期平均允许速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Refill rate is how fast tokens are added back to the bucket, setting the long-term sustained rate.

q: 把 Token Bucket 的单次检查流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put a single Token Bucket check into the correct order:
steps: 按 elapsed time 和 refill rate 补充 token，最多到 capacity
读取 client bucket 的 tokens 和 last_refill
如果 token >= 1，扣一个并允许请求
写回 tokens、last_refill，并设置 inactivity TTL
如果 token 不足，拒绝请求
why: 核心是 read-modify-write：先补充，再根据当前 token 决策，并持久化新状态。拒绝路径是否写回时间戳取决于实现，但原子边界不能拆开。
why_en: A token-bucket check reads state, refills tokens, decides allow or deny, and writes the updated state atomically.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Req[Request] --> Load[Load bucket]
Load --> Refill[Refill by elapsed time]
Refill --> Enough{Token available}
Enough -->|yes| Allow[Allow and decrement]
Enough -->|no| Deny[Return 429]

scenario: 多个 API Gateway 实例都要看到同一个用户的 token bucket 状态，且每次检查必须很快。
scenario_en: Multiple API Gateway instances must all see the same user's token-bucket state, and every check must stay fast.
q: 共享状态最合适放在哪里？
q_en: Where should the shared bucket state live?
options: 每个 gateway 的本地 map
离线数据仓库
Redis 这类内存 KV store
客户端 cookie
why: Redis 提供低延迟的跨实例共享状态、TTL 自动清理和原子脚本；只放本地会回到各 gateway 分裂计数的老问题。
why_en: Redis works as shared state because it is fast, supports TTL cleanup, and can run atomic update scripts across every gateway instance.
whenOtherWins: 单实例服务可以只用本地内存；需要长期审计分析时，应异步写日志系统，而不是挤占在线限流路径。
tradeoff: 跨实例共享一致 vs 本地内存更低的单跳延迟
options_en: A local map inside each gateway
An offline data warehouse
An in-memory KV store such as Redis
A client-side cookie
optionExplanations: 本地 map 只在一台 gateway 内部可见，多个实例之间看不到彼此的计数，又回到各扛各的老问题。
数据仓库是批量分析用的，写入和查询都有延迟，跟每次请求都要即时判断的要求对不上。
Redis 能让所有 gateway 实例共享同一份 bucket 状态，操作又是亚毫秒级，正好卡住跨实例一致又要快的要求。
状态存进客户端 cookie，用户自己就能清掉或伪造，根本挡不住真正想绕过限流的人。
optionExplanations_en: A local map is only visible inside one gateway instance — different instances still can't see each other's counts, back to the split-counting problem.
A data warehouse is built for batch analysis with write and query lag, which doesn't fit a check that needs an instant answer on every request.
Redis lets every gateway instance share the same bucket state while staying sub-millisecond, which is exactly the shared-and-fast combination this needs.
Storing state in a client cookie lets the user clear or fake it themselves — no real barrier for someone trying to dodge the limit.

scenario: gateway 要读取某用户 bucket 的 token 数和最后 refill 时间，这两个字段存放在 Redis hash 中。
scenario_en: The gateway needs to read a user's token count and last-refill time, and both fields live in a Redis hash.
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最贴合这个读取？
q_en: Which Redis command best fits this read?
options: KEYS alice:bucket:*
BLPOP alice:bucket 0
PUBLISH alice:bucket check
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
codeSample:
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
HSET alice:bucket tokens <new_token_count>
HSET alice:bucket last_refill <current_timestamp>
EXPIRE alice:bucket 3600
why: bucket 状态是一个小 hash，HMGET 能一次读出 tokens 和 last_refill 两个字段；生产实现还要把整段判断放进原子脚本。
why_en: HMGET reads multiple fields of a Redis hash in one call, which fits reading a client's tokens and last-refill time together.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态只是一个数字，INCR/DECR 可能就够；Token Bucket 需要 tokens 和 last_refill 两个字段。
tradeoff: 定向读两个字段 vs 扫描/阻塞/广播类命令的开销
options_en: KEYS alice:bucket:*
BLPOP alice:bucket 0
PUBLISH alice:bucket check
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
optionExplanations: KEYS 会扫描整个 keyspace，生产环境用它做单次读取既慢又危险。
BLPOP 是阻塞式弹出队列元素的命令，这里没有队列要处理。
PUBLISH 是发消息给订阅者，跟读取一个 hash 里的字段是两回事。
bucket 状态就是一个小 hash，HMGET 能一次调用读出 tokens 和 last_refill 两个字段。
optionExplanations_en: KEYS scans the entire keyspace — using it for a single read is slow and risky in production.
BLPOP blocks waiting to pop from a queue; there's no queue involved here.
PUBLISH sends a message to subscribers, which has nothing to do with reading fields off a hash.
The bucket state is just a small hash, and HMGET reads both the tokens and last_refill fields in one call.

q: 为什么 HMGET 后再 MULTI/HSET/EXEC 仍可能有竞态？
q_en: Why can a race condition still occur even after wrapping the write in MULTI/EXEC?
options: 读操作在事务外，两个 gateway 可能都读到旧值并放行
MULTI/EXEC 从不真正执行写入
Redis hash 里存不了时间戳
EXPIRE 会把所有用户一起删掉
why: MULTI/EXEC 只保证写入这一步原子，但读取 HMGET 发生在事务外；两个 gateway 同时读到同一个旧值时，可能都判断可放行，导致超发。
why_en: Wrapping only the write in MULTI/EXEC is not enough, because two gateways can read the same stale token count before either one writes back.
options_en: The read happens outside the transaction, so two gateways can both read a stale value and allow
MULTI/EXEC never actually performs the write
A Redis hash cannot store a timestamp
EXPIRE deletes every user's data at once

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 事务:MULTI 开始、把命令排队、EXEC 一次性原子执行,中间不被别的命令插入。但它「只让这批写原子」——不能在事务里读一个值再据此分支,所以救不了「读完再判再写」的竞态
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis transaction: MULTI queues commands and EXEC runs them atomically with no interleaving. But it only makes that batch of writes atomic — you cannot read a value and branch on it inside it, so it does not fix a read-then-decide-then-write race.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 乐观锁:WATCH 一个 key 后,若它在 EXEC 前被别人改过,整个 MULTI/EXEC 作废(EXEC 返 nil),你重试。用来补上「读到的值可能已过期」这个洞
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis optimistic locking: after WATCH a key, if it changes before EXEC the whole MULTI/EXEC aborts (EXEC returns nil) and you retry — plugging the "the value you read may be stale" hole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Redis 内部原子跑一段 Lua 脚本(Redis 单线程→脚本跑完中间无插入)。EVAL 传脚本文本;EVALSHA 传 SCRIPT LOAD 后的 SHA(省带宽)。限流就把「读+判+写」整段锁进一个脚本
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Run a Lua script atomically inside Redis (single-threaded → runs to completion with no interleaving). EVAL sends the script text; EVALSHA sends the SHA of a SCRIPT LOAD-ed script (saves bandwidth). Rate limiting locks read+decide+write into one script.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读/写 Redis hash 的字段。bucket 状态(tokens、last_refill)存成一个 hash;HMGET 一次读多个字段、HSET 写一个字段
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read/write fields of a Redis hash. Bucket state (tokens, last_refill) is stored as a hash; HMGET reads several fields at once, HSET writes one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定窗口计数最简做法:INCR key 原子 +1、EXPIRE 设窗口 TTL。坑:两条命令,崩在中间就没 TTL → 用 Lua 或 SET key 1 EX n NX 一步搞定
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The simplest fixed-window counter: INCR key (atomic +1) and EXPIRE for the window TTL. Pitfall: two commands — a crash between leaves no TTL; use Lua or SET key 1 EX n NX to do it in one step.

optionExplanations: MULTI/EXEC 只让写入这一步原子，但 HMGET 读取发生在事务外，两个 gateway 完全可能同时读到同一个旧值、都判断可以放行。
MULTI/EXEC 确实会执行写入，问题不在它执行不执行，而在读取没被包进去。
Redis hash 存时间戳完全没问题，这跟原子性问题是两件事。
EXPIRE 只清理它作用的那一个 key，不会波及其他用户，这个说法夸大了它的影响范围。
optionExplanations_en: MULTI/EXEC only makes the write atomic, but the HMGET read happens outside the transaction, so two gateways can both read the same stale value and both decide to allow.
MULTI/EXEC does actually perform the write — the problem isn't whether it runs, it's that the read isn't wrapped inside it.
A Redis hash stores a timestamp just fine — that's unrelated to the atomicity problem here.
EXPIRE only clears the one key it's applied to, not every user's data — this overstates its blast radius.
codeSample:
# ❌ 有竞态:「读→判断→写」是分开三步,MULTI 只保证「写」原子
count = HMGET rl:u1 tokens            # 两个 gateway 都读到 tokens=1
if count > 0:                         # 都判「可放行」
    MULTI; HSET rl:u1 tokens 0; EXEC  # 都写 0 → 两个都放行 = 超发!

# ✅ 修法1 WATCH(乐观锁):key 在 EXEC 前被改就整体作废、重试
WATCH rl:u1
count = HGET rl:u1 tokens
MULTI; HSET rl:u1 tokens count-1; EXEC   # 期间 key 变了 → EXEC 返 nil → 重试

# ✅ 修法2 EVAL Lua(最常用):读+判+写在一个脚本里原子跑
EVAL "local c=tonumber(redis.call('HGET',KEYS[1],'tokens'))
      if c>0 then redis.call('HSET',KEYS[1],'tokens',c-1); return 1
      else return 0 end" 1 rl:u1

rows: 多轮往返 + 重试循环

scenario: 需要让读取 bucket、计算 refill、扣 token、写回状态在 Redis 里成为一个不可 interleave 的操作。
scenario_en: Reading the bucket, computing the refill, decrementing a token, and writing the state back all need to become one non-interleavable operation in Redis.
q: 应该使用什么机制？
q_en: What mechanism should be used?
options: 客户端 sleep 10ms
Redis Lua script
两个独立 HTTP 请求
只依赖 EXPIRE
codeSample:
-- EVAL rate_limit.lua alice:bucket now refill capacity
local tokens = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens')
-- calculate refill, decide allow, HSET new fields atomically
return {allowed, remaining, resetTime}
why: Lua 脚本在 Redis 内部一次性原子执行，能把读取、计算、写回整段逻辑锁进一个不可 interleave 的操作，正是解决计数竞态的关键。
why_en: A Redis Lua script runs the whole read-calculate-write sequence as one atomic step inside Redis, closing the race window.
whenOtherWins: 简单固定窗口可以用 INCR+EXPIRE 这类单命令模式；Token Bucket 的计算更适合放进脚本。
tradeoff: 整段 read-modify-write 原子 vs 多命令往返的竞态风险
diagram:
flowchart LR
Gateway[Gateway] --> Lua[Redis Lua script]
Lua --> Read[Read tokens]
Lua --> Update[Refill and decrement]
Lua --> Result[Allow or deny]
options_en: The client sleeps 10ms
A Redis Lua script
Two independent HTTP requests
Rely only on EXPIRE

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 支持在服务端原子执行的小脚本，可以把多步逻辑合并成一次调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script lets Redis execute multiple steps atomically on the server in a single call.

optionExplanations: 让客户端自己 sleep 10ms 完全不影响 Redis 里那几步读改写会不会被别的请求插进来，解决不了真正的竞态。
Lua 脚本在 Redis 内部一次性跑完读取、算 refill、扣 token、写回，中间不会被其他请求插队。
拆成两次独立 HTTP 请求，中间还是留了个窗口，两个 gateway 完全可能在这个窗口里都读到旧值。
EXPIRE 只负责清理长时间不用的 key，管不住同一时刻多个请求并发读改写同一个 bucket。
optionExplanations_en: Having the client sleep 10ms does nothing to stop another request from interleaving with the read-modify-write inside Redis — it doesn't close the race.
A Lua script runs the read, refill calculation, decrement, and write back inside Redis in one shot, with no other request able to interleave.
Splitting it into two separate HTTP requests still leaves a gap in between, and two gateways can easily both read the old value inside that gap.
EXPIRE only cleans up a key after it sits unused for a while — it does nothing about several requests concurrently reading and writing the same bucket at once.

q: Redis 适合限流状态的原因有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Why does Redis fit rate-limit state well? (multi-select)
options: 简单操作亚毫秒级
EXPIRE 可清理不活跃 bucket
支持复制/高可用
Lua 等机制支持原子操作
why: 限流状态小、热、生命周期短：Redis 的亚毫秒操作、EXPIRE 自动清理、复制/HA 和 Lua 原子脚本都贴合这个场景。
why_en: Redis fits rate-limit state because it is fast, supports TTL cleanup, can be replicated for availability, and can run atomic scripts.
options_en: Simple operations run in sub-millisecond time
EXPIRE cleans up inactive buckets
It supports replication for high availability
Mechanisms like Lua support atomic operations
optionExplanations: 简单的 GET/SET 级操作能做到亚毫秒，检查一次限流不会拖慢整条请求路径。
EXPIRE 让不活跃 client 的 bucket 自动被清理，不用额外写一个定时清理任务。
支持复制和主从切换，Redis 本身挂了不至于让整个限流层跟着停摆。
Lua 脚本能把读取、计算、写回锁进一次原子调用，解决多网关并发更新同一个 bucket 的竞态。
optionExplanations_en: Simple GET/SET-level operations run in sub-millisecond time, so a check doesn't slow down the request path.
EXPIRE lets an inactive client's bucket clean itself up automatically, no separate cleanup job needed.
Replication and automatic failover mean a single Redis node dying doesn't take the whole rate-limit layer down with it.
A Lua script locks the read, refill, and write into one atomic call, which closes the race window when multiple gateways update the same bucket concurrently.

scenario: 用户已经超出限制；这是交互式 API，请求排队会消耗资源并让响应时间不可预测。
scenario_en: A user has already exceeded the limit; this is an interactive API, and queuing requests would burn resources and make latency unpredictable.
q: 超限请求应该如何处理？
q_en: How should an over-limit request be handled?
options: 排队到窗口重置后再处理
静默丢弃无响应
fail fast，立即返回 HTTP 429
把请求写入长期数据库等待人工处理
why: 交互式 API 超限时立刻返回更可控：客户端能照 headers 退避重试。排队会占内存、诱发重复重试，还让响应时间变得不可预测。
why_en: Interactive APIs should fail fast with a 429 instead of queuing, because queued requests waste memory and make latency unpredictable.
whenOtherWins: 批处理或后台作业能接受排队等待；用户正在等待响应的交互式 API 通常不适合。
tradeoff: 立即失败、延迟可预测 vs 排队等待、更友好但更不可控
options_en: Queue the request until the window resets
Silently drop it with no response
Fail fast and return HTTP 429 immediately
Write it to a long-term database for manual review
optionExplanations: 把超限请求挂起等窗口重置，等待时间不可控，还会占着连接和内存，交互式场景等不起。
直接丢掉不给任何响应，客户端只会当成超时不断重试，比明确拒绝更浪费资源。
立刻返回 429 加上 headers，客户端能马上知道被拒了、该等多久，延迟可预测。
把超限请求丢进数据库等人工处理，跟这是一个交互式在线请求的前提完全不匹配，用户等不到那个时候。
optionExplanations_en: Queuing an over-limit request until the window resets makes wait time unpredictable and still ties up connections and memory — an interactive API can't afford that.
Dropping the request with no response just looks like a timeout to the client, which then keeps retrying — wasting more resources than a clear rejection would.
Returning 429 with headers immediately tells the client right away that it was rejected and how long to wait, keeping latency predictable.
Writing an over-limit request to a database for manual review doesn't fit an interactive request at all — the user won't still be waiting by the time anyone looks at it.

q: HTTP 429 响应中常见的有用 headers 有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which headers are commonly useful on an HTTP 429 response? (multi-select)
options: X-RateLimit-Limit
X-RateLimit-Remaining
X-RateLimit-Reset
Retry-After
why: 这些 header 把限额、剩余额度、重置时间和建议等待时间都告诉客户端，好的客户端据此退避，而不是继续硬打 API。
why_en: Rate-limit headers tell the client the ceiling, remaining quota, reset time, and how long to wait before retrying.
options_en: X-RateLimit-Limit
X-RateLimit-Remaining
X-RateLimit-Reset
Retry-After
optionExplanations: X-RateLimit-Limit 告诉客户端这条规则总配额是多少，方便它自己算节奏。
X-RateLimit-Remaining 是这次请求后还剩多少次，客户端能据此判断要不要放慢。
X-RateLimit-Reset 给出配额什么时候刷新，客户端可以掐着这个时间点再试。
Retry-After 直接给出建议等待秒数，是最省心的退避依据。
optionExplanations_en: X-RateLimit-Limit tells the client the total quota for this rule, so it can pace itself.
X-RateLimit-Remaining shows how many calls are left after this one, letting the client decide whether to slow down.
X-RateLimit-Reset gives the moment the quota refreshes, so the client can time its next attempt.
Retry-After gives a straight suggested wait in seconds — the simplest signal to back off by.

scenario: 请求被拒绝，客户端需要明确知道为什么失败以及何时重试。
scenario_en: A request is rejected, and the client needs to clearly know why it failed and when to retry.
q: 哪种响应最符合规范和用户体验？
q_en: Which response best matches the HTTP spec and gives a good client experience?
options: 返回 HTTP 200 成功状态，只在 body 里说明 error
返回 HTTP 500 服务器错误，且不附带任何 header
不返回任何响应，让客户端连接持续挂起
HTTP 429 + X-RateLimit-* + Retry-After
codeSample:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640995200
Retry-After: 60
why: 429 是 Too Many Requests 的标准状态码，配合限额/剩余/重置 headers 能让客户端正确退避；不要用 200 或 500 掩盖限流语义。
why_en: A proper 429 response with rate-limit headers lets well-behaved clients understand the rejection and back off correctly.
whenOtherWins: 内部批处理协议可以用自定义错误码；面向公众的 HTTP API 应该遵守标准 429 语义。
tradeoff: 遵守 HTTP 语义方便客户端退避 vs 伪装成 200/500 让客户端困惑
options_en: Return HTTP 200 success and put the error only in the body
Return HTTP 500 with no headers at all
Send no response and leave the connection hanging
HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After
optionExplanations: 把限流拒绝包装成 HTTP 200，客户端的正常成功逻辑会直接把这次拒绝当成功处理，完全错判。
500 意味着服务器出错，但限流拒绝其实是预期行为，用错误码还不给 header，客户端连该等多久都不知道。
完全不响应会让客户端的连接一直悬着，最后大概率触发超时重试，比直接告诉它被拒还差。
429 是标准的 Too Many Requests 状态码，配合 X-RateLimit-* 和 Retry-After，客户端能照着退避重试。
optionExplanations_en: Wrapping a rate-limit rejection in an HTTP 200 makes the client's normal success path treat a rejection as a success — completely misread.
500 signals a server error, but a rate-limit rejection is expected behavior; using the wrong code with no headers also leaves the client with no idea how long to wait.
Sending no response at all just leaves the client's connection hanging, likely triggering a timeout retry — worse than telling it plainly that it was rejected.
429 is the standard Too Many Requests status, and pairing it with X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After gives the client exactly what it needs to back off correctly.

scenario: 单个 Redis 实例的典型操作吞吐约 100k-200k ops/sec，而一次限流检查至少要读一次、写一次。
scenario_en: A single Redis instance typically handles about 100k-200k ops/sec, and each rate-limit check needs at least one read and one write.
q: 这对能否用一个 Redis 实例支撑 1M requests/sec 的限流检查意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply about supporting 1M requests/sec of rate-limit checks on a single Redis instance?
options: 不够：实际检查吞吐远低于 1M/sec，必须分片到多个实例
足够：单实例可以直接扛住 1M/sec
应该放弃 Redis，改成查询主数据库计数
应该把 refill rate 设为 0 来减轻压力
why: 一次检查至少 1 读 1 写，单实例约 100k-200k ops/sec 换算下来大概只能撑 50k-100k 次检查/sec，离 1M 差一个数量级，必须分片。
why_en: Because each check needs a read and a write, a single Redis instance realistically handles tens of thousands of checks per second, not a million, so sharding is required.
options_en: Not enough: real check throughput is far below 1M/sec, so it must be sharded
Enough: a single instance can directly handle 1M/sec
Abandon Redis and count against the primary database instead
Set the refill rate to zero to reduce load
optionExplanations: 一次检查至少 1 读 1 写，单实例约 100k-200k ops/sec 换算成检查次数大概只有几万到十万级，离 1M 差了一个数量级，必须分片。
把单实例的 ops/sec 直接当成检查次数用，忽略了一次检查要占两次操作，这个换算是错的。
主数据库的单次读写延迟通常比 Redis 高一个数量级，换成它只会让瓶颈更严重。
把 refill rate 设成 0 意味着所有请求都会一直被拒绝，这是把限流器变成了断路器，没有解决吞吐问题。
optionExplanations_en: Each check needs at least one read and one write, so a single instance's roughly 100k-200k ops/sec only covers tens of thousands of checks per second — an order of magnitude short of 1M, so sharding is required.
Treating a single instance's raw ops/sec as its check throughput ignores that each check costs two operations — that conversion is wrong.
A primary database's per-operation latency is usually an order of magnitude worse than Redis, so switching to it would make the bottleneck worse, not better.
Setting the refill rate to zero means every request gets rejected forever — that turns the limiter into a circuit breaker, not a fix for throughput.

scenario: 目标是 1M RPS，单 Redis 实例成为瓶颈；同一 client 的请求必须始终命中同一份 bucket 状态。
scenario_en: The target is 1M RPS and a single Redis instance is the bottleneck; the same client's requests must always hit the same bucket state.
q: Redis 状态应该如何扩展？
q_en: How should Redis state be scaled out?
options: 随机挑一个 Redis 实例写入状态
按 client identifier 一致性哈希到固定 shard
把同一份 bucket 复制到所有 shard 后随便读写
每个请求都广播给全部 Redis 实例
why: 按 client identifier 一致性哈希，保证同一 client 永远落在同一 shard，同时把负载摊开；Redis Cluster 可用 hash slot 自动路由。
why_en: Sharding by client identifier keeps each client's rate-limit state on one Redis shard while spreading different clients' load across shards.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则是全局总 QPS 而不是按 client，需要单独的全局或分层计数机制。
tradeoff: 同一 client 状态集中在一个 shard vs 全局总量类规则难以直接分片
options_en: Write to a randomly chosen Redis instance
Consistent-hash the client identifier onto a fixed shard
Copy the same bucket to every shard and read/write any of them
Broadcast every request to all Redis instances

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种让 key 稳定映射到某个节点、且扩缩容时只影响少量 key 的哈希方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps each key to a stable node so that adding or removing nodes only reshuffles a small fraction of keys.

optionExplanations: 每次随机挑一个实例写状态，同一个 client 的请求可能这次落在 shard A、下次落在 shard B，计数根本对不上。
按 client identifier 一致性哈希，保证同一个 client 永远落在同一个 shard，同时把不同 client 的负载摊开到多个实例。
把同一份 bucket 复制到所有 shard 后随便读写，等于放弃了单一权威副本，写冲突谁也说不清。
每个请求都广播给全部实例，等于把总请求量乘上实例数，反而制造出新的瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Writing to a randomly chosen instance each time means the same client's requests can land on shard A once and shard B next time — the count never adds up.
Consistent-hashing the client identifier keeps a given client permanently on one shard while spreading different clients' load across many instances.
Copying the same bucket to every shard and letting any of them write it abandons a single source of truth — write conflicts become unresolvable.
Broadcasting every request to all instances multiplies total traffic by the instance count, creating a brand-new bottleneck instead of fixing one.

q: 补全 Redis Cluster 的分片机制：
q_en: Fill in how Redis Cluster shards data:
text: Redis Cluster 把 keyspace 切成 {{16384}} 个 hash slots，并把这些 slots 分配到多个 Redis nodes。
why: 使用 Redis Cluster 时，gateway 不必自己维护一致性哈希细节，客户端/集群会根据 key 的 slot 自动路由到正确的节点。
why_en: Redis Cluster shards keys across 16,384 hash slots distributed over multiple nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 用来分配 key 归属节点的一个编号区间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash slot is a numbered bucket Redis Cluster uses to decide which node owns a key.

scenario: 每个 Redis shard 约能处理 100k checks/sec；目标总吞吐是 1M checks/sec。
scenario_en: Each Redis shard handles about 100k checks/sec, and the target total throughput is 1M checks/sec.
q: 要达到这个目标吞吐，Redis 状态应该怎么部署？
q_en: How should Redis state be deployed to hit this target throughput?
options: 继续用单实例，靠升级硬件解决
关闭一部分限流规则来降低压力
按 client key 分片到约 10 个实例
把所有数据复制到每个节点本地判断
why: 1M / 100k ≈ 10，量级上需要十几个 shard 而不是一个大实例；真实生产还要再加副本和余量。
why_en: One million divided by about 100k checks per shard is roughly ten shards, plus replicas and headroom in production.
options_en: Keep a single instance and just upgrade hardware
Turn off some rate-limit rules to reduce load
Shard state by client key across about ten instances
Copy all data to every node and decide locally
optionExplanations: 硬件升级能小幅提升单实例的吞吐上限，但离 10 倍差距还差得远，量级上解决不了问题。
关掉规则等于放弃限流本身要保护的东西，不是解决吞吐瓶颈的办法。
1M / 100k ≈ 10，量级上大概需要十个左右的 shard，而不是继续加大单个实例。
把所有数据复制到每个节点，写入要同步到所有副本，反而会把单点的写入压力放大成全网压力。
optionExplanations_en: Upgrading hardware can nudge a single instance's ceiling up a bit, but it's nowhere close to a 10x gap — it doesn't fix the order-of-magnitude problem.
Turning off rules gives up the very protection rate limiting exists for — it doesn't address the throughput bottleneck.
One million divided by roughly 100k per shard is about ten shards — the fix is spreading out, not growing one instance further.
Copying all data to every node means each write has to sync to every replica, turning what was one instance's write pressure into pressure across the whole cluster.

q: 把分片限流检查流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the sharded rate-limit check flow into the correct order:
steps: gateway 提取 userId/IP/API key 作为 identifier
Redis shard 内原子执行 Token Bucket 判断
对 identifier 做 consistent hash 或计算 Redis slot
根据结果返回 passes/remaining/resetTime
把请求路由到负责该 identifier 的 Redis shard
why: identifier 是分片键，必须稳定映射到同一 shard。到达 shard 后，算法本身和单实例 Token Bucket 基本一样。
why_en: The gateway extracts a stable identifier, routes it to the owning Redis shard, and runs the token-bucket decision there atomically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Req[Request key] --> Hash[Hash key]
Hash --> Shard[Redis shard]
Shard --> Lua[Atomic check]
Lua --> Decision[Allow or 429]

q: fail-closed 的含义是什么？
q_en: What does fail-closed mean?
options: 限流器故障时改为放行所有请求
只对已付费的用户执行限流
把超限请求排队等 Redis 恢复
无法判断时拒绝请求，保护后端但牺牲可用性
why: fail-closed 保守：判断不了就拒绝，保护后端但会牺牲可用性——健康的请求也可能被挡在门外。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects requests it cannot verify, protecting backends at the cost of rejecting some healthy traffic too.
tradeoff: 保护后端优先 vs 可用性优先
options_en: Switch to allowing all requests when the limiter fails
Only rate-limit paying customers
Queue over-limit requests until Redis recovers
Reject requests it cannot verify, protecting the backend at the cost of availability
optionExplanations: 故障时改成放行所有请求，说的其实是 fail-open 的定义，跟这里问的正好相反。
只挑付费用户限流是一个业务规则的选择，跟「故障时怎么办」这个 fail-closed 的定义没有关系。
把超限请求挂起排队，是另一种处理策略，不是 fail-closed 这个术语本身的定义。
判断不了配额时选择拒绝而不是放行，这样能护住后端，但代价是一些本该通过的健康请求也会被挡在门外。
optionExplanations_en: Switching to allow everything on failure is actually the definition of fail-open — the opposite of what's being asked here.
Rate-limiting only paying users is a business-rule choice, unrelated to what fail-closed means about handling a failure.
Queuing over-limit requests until Redis recovers is a different handling strategy, not the definition of the term fail-closed itself.
Choosing to reject rather than allow when quota can't be verified protects the backend, at the cost of also blocking some healthy requests that should have gone through.

q: fail-open 的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of fail-open?
options: Redis 不可用时流量直通后端，高峰可能引发级联故障
它会把所有健康请求也一起拒绝掉
它反而让限流判断更加精确
它要求每个客户端自己实现 Lua 脚本
why: fail-open 保住了可用性，但暂时失去限流保护；如果 Redis 正是因为流量或攻击才出问题，放开闸门可能直接压垮后端。
why_en: Fail-open keeps the API available but removes protection at the exact moment traffic or an attack may already be overwhelming the backend.
tradeoff: 可用性优先 vs 失去保护窗口
options_en: When Redis is unavailable, all traffic passes straight through and can cascade during a spike
It rejects every healthy request as well
It makes rate-limit decisions more precise
It requires every client to implement Lua itself
optionExplanations: Redis 不可用时流量直通后端，如果高峰或攻击流量正好赶上这个时候，后端可能被直接压垮，引发级联故障。
拒绝所有健康请求说的是 fail-closed 的行为，fail-open 恰恰相反，是继续放行。
fail-open 时限流器已经不工作了，谈不上判断更精确，反而是完全没有判断。
Lua 脚本是服务端 Redis 里的实现细节，跟客户端要不要自己实现什么完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: When Redis is down, traffic passes straight through, and if that coincides with a traffic spike or an attack, the backend can get overwhelmed, triggering a cascading failure.
Rejecting every healthy request describes fail-closed behavior — fail-open does the opposite and keeps letting traffic through.
Under fail-open the limiter has effectively stopped working, so there's no decision being made at all, let alone a more precise one.
The Lua script is a server-side Redis implementation detail, unrelated to whether clients need to implement anything themselves.

scenario: 社交平台在 viral 事件中流量突增；Redis-based 限流层故障或超时，系统无法可靠读取/更新计数，而后端数据库和应用也可能已经接近容量上限。
scenario_en: A social platform sees a traffic surge during a viral event; the Redis-based limiter fails or times out so counts can't be reliably read or updated, and the backend database and app are already near capacity.
q: 此时最直接选择哪种失败模式？
q_en: Which failure mode is the right call here?
options: fail-open
fail-closed
无限排队
客户端自觉限流即可
why: fail-closed = 限流器不可用时默认拒绝或降级拦截；在后端已接近容量时，它牺牲一部分可用性来避免流量绕过限流打爆数据库。fail-open = 限流器不可用时默认放行，用户可用性更高，但可能把 Redis 故障放大成级联故障。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects or degrades requests when the limiter is unavailable, protecting a near-capacity backend from a Redis outage becoming a cascading failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果后端余量很大、限流只是软配额或非关键保护，fail-open 更适合，因为它优先保证用户请求继续成功。
tradeoff: 下游保护/防级联故障 vs 用户可用性
options_en: Fail-open
Fail-closed
Queue requests indefinitely
Rely on client-side limiting alone

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认放行请求；在限流场景里，就是 Redis/限流器超时或不可用时仍让请求进入后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-open means allowing requests by default when the protective component fails, such as letting traffic through when Redis rate limiting times out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认拒绝或降级拦截请求；在限流场景里，就是无法判断配额时返回 429/503 或走保守拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-closed means rejecting or degrading requests by default when the protective component fails, such as returning 429 or 503 when quota cannot be checked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个组件故障后，流量、重试或负载转移继续压垮下游组件，导致故障范围扩大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading failure is when one component failure shifts load or retries onto downstream components until more of the system fails.

optionExplanations: fail-open 会在限流器故障时默认放行，用户成功率更高，但这里后端已经接近容量，放行会让绕过限流的流量直接冲垮它，级联风险太大。
fail-closed 在无法判断配额时默认拒绝，会挡住一部分健康请求，但优先保护已经吃紧的后端不被打垮，是这里更安全的选择。
把请求无限期挂起等 Redis 恢复，只会在入口层堆积连接、线程和内存，往往比直接快速失败更危险。
把限流责任丢给客户端本身不难实现，但攻击者或异常客户端不会乖乖配合，服务端失去了强制手段。
optionExplanations_en: Fail-open keeps the API available by default when the limiter breaks, but here the backend is already near capacity, so letting traffic bypass the limiter risks tipping it into cascading failure.
Fail-closed rejects requests it can't verify, blocking some healthy traffic, but that protects an already-stressed backend from being overwhelmed — the safer call here.
Queuing requests indefinitely until Redis recovers just piles up connections, threads, and memory at the entry layer, usually more dangerous than failing fast.
Handing rate limiting to the client is easy to build, but attackers or buggy clients won't reliably cooperate, so the server loses its only enforcement point.

scenario: Redis 已按 client 分片，但任一 shard 挂掉会影响其负责的一批用户；希望自动恢复写能力。
scenario_en: Redis is already sharded by client, but any shard going down affects the batch of users it owns; the goal is automatic recovery of write capability.
q: 标准高可用方案是什么？
q_en: What is the standard high-availability approach?
options: 只用单 master，完全不配副本
把 bucket 状态写进浏览器本地存储
每个 shard 配副本，故障时自动提升
每次故障都靠人工手动切换 Redis
why: master-replica 复制加自动 failover 是标准做法，Redis Cluster 能自动探测故障并提升副本；代价是成本和短暂复制延迟。
why_en: Standard Redis high availability uses master-replica replication with automatic promotion on failure, at the cost of extra infrastructure and brief replication lag.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统能接受单实例故障；跨地域强隔离需求可能要每区域独立集群加更复杂策略。
tradeoff: 自动故障恢复 vs 额外副本成本和复制延迟
options_en: Use a single master with no replicas at all
Write bucket state into the browser's local storage
Give every shard a replica and auto-promote it on failure
Fail over by hand every single time
optionExplanations: 只有一个 master、不配副本，它一旦挂掉，负责的那批用户的限流状态就直接不可用了。
把状态存进用户浏览器本地，用户换设备、清缓存都能重置额度，根本挡不住真正想绕过限流的人。
每个 shard 配副本，master 挂了副本自动顶上，恢复写能力不用等人来手动切换。
每次故障都靠人手动切，从发现到真正切换完的这段时间，那批用户的限流写入完全没人管。
optionExplanations_en: A single master with no replica means the moment it dies, the whole batch of users it owned lose their rate-limit state entirely.
Storing state in the user's browser local storage lets them reset their quota just by switching devices or clearing cache — no real barrier against someone trying to dodge the limit.
Giving every shard a replica that auto-promotes on failure restores write capability without waiting for a human to step in.
Failing over by hand leaves a gap between the moment a shard dies and someone actually completing the switch, during which that batch of users has no working rate-limit writes at all.

q: 限流系统应监控哪些指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metrics should a rate-limiting system monitor? (multi-select)
options: Redis CPU、内存、网络连通性
限流检查成功率和延迟
进入 fail-open/fail-closed 降级模式的事件
每个用户的头像颜色
why: 限流器挡在请求入口，必须能快速发现 Redis 异常、决策延迟升高或降级模式被触发；跟限流健康无关的指标不该混进来。
why_en: Rate-limiter observability should cover Redis health, check latency and success rate, and transitions into fail-open or fail-closed.
options_en: Redis CPU, memory, and network connectivity
Rate-limit check success rate and latency
Events entering fail-open or fail-closed degraded mode
Every user's avatar color
optionExplanations: Redis CPU、内存、网络这些底层健康指标出问题，限流检查会先变慢甚至直接失败。
限流检查成功率和延迟直接反映这道入口关卡本身有没有在正常工作。
进入 fail-open/fail-closed 的事件要单独监控，因为一旦触发就意味着系统正在用降级模式运行。
用户头像颜色跟限流系统健不健康没有任何关系，混进监控面板只会增加噪音。
optionExplanations_en: Redis CPU, memory, and network health degrading is usually the first sign a rate-limit check is about to slow down or fail.
Check success rate and latency directly show whether this entry-point gate is working normally.
Transitions into fail-open or fail-closed deserve their own alert, because hitting either one means the system is already running in a degraded mode.
A user's avatar color has nothing to do with whether the limiter is healthy — it's just noise on the dashboard.

scenario: 每次限流检查都要访问 Redis；如果 gateway 每次都新建 TCP 连接，额外握手会让请求延迟不可接受。
scenario_en: Every rate-limit check hits Redis; if the gateway opens a new TCP connection each time, the extra handshake makes request latency unacceptable.
q: 最重要的低延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the single most important low-latency optimization?
options: 每请求打开新连接以避免复用
把限流检查改成离线批处理
删除所有 headers
连接池 / 持久 Redis 连接
why: 连接池复用已建立的 TCP 连接，省掉每次 20-50ms 级别的握手开销；Redis 操作本身很快，连接管理常常才是主要延迟来源。
why_en: Connection pooling reuses established TCP connections and avoids repeated handshake overhead on the hot path.
whenOtherWins: 很低频的管理接口可以用简单短连接；核心请求路径必须复用连接。
tradeoff: 复用连接省握手延迟 vs 每次新建连接的简单但慢
options_en: Open a fresh connection per request to avoid reuse
Turn rate-limit checks into an offline batch job
Strip out all response headers
Connection pooling with persistent Redis connections

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一组已建立的连接，而不是每次请求都重新握手。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection pooling reuses a set of already-open connections instead of opening a new one per request.

optionExplanations: 每个请求都开新连接，意味着每次都要重新走一次 TCP 握手，这正是要避免的延迟来源，不是优化。
把限流检查改成离线批处理，请求进来时根本等不到判断结果，这跟「低延迟在线检查」的前提直接冲突。
删掉 headers 省不了访问 Redis 的那次网络往返，跟连接开销完全不是一回事。
连接池复用已经建立好的 TCP 连接，省掉每次新建连接的握手开销，而 Redis 操作本身已经够快，连接管理常常才是真正的延迟大头。
optionExplanations_en: Opening a fresh connection per request means redoing the TCP handshake every single time — that's exactly the latency source to avoid, not an optimization.
Turning the check into an offline batch job means a live request has nothing to wait on for its answer — it directly conflicts with needing a low-latency online check.
Stripping out headers doesn't save the network round trip to Redis at all — that's an unrelated cost from connection overhead.

Connection pooling reuses TCP connections that are already open, skipping the handshake each time, and since the Redis operation itself is already fast, connection management is often the real latency driver.

scenario: 用户分布全球；东京用户如果每次限流都访问弗吉尼亚 Redis，会多出明显网络延迟。
scenario_en: Users are distributed globally; if a Tokyo user's every rate-limit check hits Redis in Virginia, that adds noticeable network latency.
q: 最大的地理延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest optimization for geographic latency?
options: 多区域部署 Gateway 和 Redis，就近完成限流
把所有流量强制回源到单一区域
只增加 HTTP 429 的 body 字段
直接关闭 TLS 加密传输
why: 限流状态放到离用户近的区域能省掉跨洋 RTT；代价是跨区域一致性更复杂，但限流通常可以接受区域间最终一致。
why_en: Deploying gateways and Redis regionally keeps rate-limit checks close to users and avoids cross-continent round trips.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须全局强一致限额，需要单一权威区域或分层协调，但会牺牲延迟。
options_en: Deploy gateways and Redis regionally, so checks stay local
Force all traffic back to a single origin region
Just add another field to the 429 response body
Simply turn off TLS encryption
optionExplanations: 把 Gateway 和 Redis 都部署到离用户近的区域，限流检查就不用跨洋来回，直接省掉大部分 RTT。
把所有流量强制送回单一区域处理，等于把每个东京用户的请求都拖上一趟跨洋往返，延迟问题完全没解决。
只改 429 响应体里的字段跟网络距离毫无关系，请求依然要先跑到远端 Redis 才能拿到判断结果。
去掉传输层加密顶多省一点点握手开销，跨大洲的物理传播时延才是真正的瓶颈，这里根本没打中点子。
optionExplanations_en: Deploying gateways and Redis regionally keeps each check local, so it skips most of that cross-ocean round trip.
Forcing all traffic back to one origin region still sends every Tokyo request on the same long round trip — it doesn't fix the latency.
Changing a field in the 429 response body has nothing to do with network distance; the request still has to reach the far-away Redis first.
Turning off TLS only trims a bit of handshake time — the real bottleneck is physical propagation delay across continents, so this misses the point.

q: 除连接池和地理部署外，文章提到哪些可选优化？（多选）
q_en: Besides connection pooling and geographic deployment, which optional optimizations does the article mention? (multi-select)
options: 每次请求都查询中央配置数据库
Redis pipelining 或 Lua scripts 减少往返
同用户突发请求的 request batching
本地缓存限流状态但要小心 stale
why: pipelining/Lua 减少往返，batching 摊薄热点请求，本地缓存要小心 stale；但每次查中央配置库会直接拖垮延迟目标，不该走这条路。
why_en: Pipelining, Lua scripts, careful batching, and cautious local caching can cut latency, while querying a central config database on every request would not.
options_en: Querying a central config database on every request
Redis pipelining or Lua scripts to cut round trips
Batching a burst of requests from the same user
Local caching of rate-limit state, done carefully to avoid staleness
optionExplanations: 每个请求都去查一次中央配置库，等于给本来要省的那次 Redis 往返重新加回一次数据库往返，直接违背低延迟目标。
pipelining 或 Lua 脚本把多条命令并成一次往返，省掉网络本身的排队和握手开销。
把同一用户短时间内的多个请求合并检查，能摊薄高频突发场景下的调用次数。
本地缓存限流状态能省掉一次网络调用，但要设好较短的刷新间隔，否则本地看到的配额会跟 Redis 里的真实值脱节。
optionExplanations_en: Querying a central config database on every request just re-adds the round trip you were trying to save, working against the latency goal.
Pipelining or Lua scripts fold several commands into one round trip, cutting network queueing and handshake overhead.
Batching several of the same user's requests together thins out the call count during a high-frequency burst.
Caching rate-limit state locally saves a network call, but needs a short refresh interval, or the local view drifts away from what Redis actually has.

q: Rate Limiter 中的 hot key 通常意味着什么？
q_en: What does a hot key usually mean in a rate limiter?
options: 某篇帖子被非常多不同用户同时读取
单个 client 请求量极高，压垮所在 shard
某张数据库表的 schema 设计得不好
所有用户的请求量都完全均匀
why: 限流状态按 client key 分片，所以 hot key 就是某一个 client 自己的请求量极大；可能是滥用攻击，也可能是合法高流量客户或 NAT 聚合。
why_en: A rate-limiter hot key is one client identifier sending enough traffic to overload the single shard that owns it.
options_en: One post is being read by many different users
One client sends extreme traffic and overloads its shard
A database table has a poorly designed schema
Every user's request volume is perfectly even
optionExplanations: 很多人读同一篇帖子是缓存场景里的热点 key，跟这里按 client 分片的限流状态是两回事。
限流状态按 client key 分片，hot key 就是某一个 client 自己的请求量极大，压垮了它所在的那个 shard。
hot key 是流量分布的问题，跟数据库表结构设计得好不好没有关系。
如果所有用户请求量都完全均匀，压根就不会出现某个 shard 被压垮的 hot key 问题。
optionExplanations_en: Many people reading the same post is the hot-key pattern in a caching scenario, a different thing from rate-limit state sharded by client.
Rate-limit state is sharded by client key, so a hot key here means one client sending extreme traffic and overloading the single shard that owns it.
A hot key is about traffic distribution, unrelated to whether a database table's schema is well designed.
If every user's traffic were perfectly even, there'd be no hot-key problem overloading a single shard in the first place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 key 承受了不成比例的巨量请求。限流里=某个 client(状态按其 key 分片)请求量极大,所有计数都砸向它所在的那一个 shard、把该 shard 压垮(别的 shard 却闲着)。成因:合法大客户 / 攻击滥用 / NAT 把很多人聚成一个 IP。缓解:各 gateway 本地预计数+周期同步,或把热 key 拆成 key+随机后缀分散到多 shard 再求和
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key takes a disproportionate share of traffic. In rate limiting it means one client (sharded by its key) sends huge volume, so all its counter ops hit the single shard owning it and overload it while others idle. Causes: a big legit customer, an attacker, or NAT aggregating many users into one IP. Mitigate with local pre-counting + periodic sync, or splitting the hot key into key+random-suffix sub-keys across shards and summing.

q: 对合法高流量 client，文章建议哪些处理方式？（多选）
q_en: For legitimate high-volume clients, which approaches does the article recommend? (multi-select)
options: 鼓励 client-side rate limiting 平滑流量
立刻永久封禁所有高流量 client
提供 batch API 减少检查次数
premium tiers 或 dedicated infrastructure
why: 合法高流量要引导承载，不是一刀切封禁：客户端限流平滑流量，批处理减少检查次数，付费/专用资源隔离压力。
why_en: Legitimate high-volume clients are handled with client-side limiting, batch APIs, or premium and dedicated infrastructure rather than blanket bans.
options_en: Encourage client-side rate limiting to smooth traffic
Permanently ban every high-volume client immediately
Offer a batch API to cut the number of checks
Offer premium tiers or dedicated infrastructure
optionExplanations: 鼓励客户端自己做限流，能把突发请求磨平成平滑曲线，减少一上来就撞限额被拒的情况。
对合法高流量客户直接永久封禁，等于把付费大客户当攻击者处理，业务上根本行不通。
提供 batch API 把多次调用合成一次，直接减少要检查的请求数量本身。
给这类客户开 premium tier 或专用基础设施，把它们的压力从共享资源池里挪出去。
optionExplanations_en: Encouraging client-side limiting smooths out bursts into a steadier curve, so fewer requests slam straight into the limit and bounce.
Permanently banning a legitimate high-volume client immediately treats a paying customer like an attacker, which doesn't work as a business move.
A batch API folds several calls into one, cutting the actual number of requests that need checking.
Giving these clients a premium tier or dedicated infrastructure moves their load out of the shared resource pool entirely.

q: 对滥用或攻击流量，哪些策略合理？（多选）
q_en: For abusive or attack traffic, which strategies are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 持续触发限流后临时加入 blocklist
使用 Cloudflare/AWS Shield 等 DDoS 防护在更前面挡流量
完全依赖客户端自觉
降低 IP-based 规则对 NAT 的误伤并更多依赖 authenticated user limit
why: 恶意流量不能指望客户端自觉，应尽早用 blocklist 和上游 DDoS 防护挡住；共享 IP 也可能是合法 NAT，IP 规则要谨慎、多依赖已登录用户限额。
why_en: Abusive traffic needs blocklists and upstream DDoS protection, while IP-based rules must stay cautious about shared NATs.
options_en: Temporarily blocklist a client after it repeatedly hits limits
Use upstream DDoS protection such as Cloudflare or AWS Shield
Rely entirely on client good behavior
Ease IP-based rules for NAT and lean more on authenticated user limits
optionExplanations: 持续触发限流的 client 先临时拉黑一段时间，比每次都放行再拒绝更省资源。
Cloudflare/AWS Shield 这类上游防护能在流量到达自己的 Redis 之前就先挡一层，减轻后面限流的压力。
完全指望客户端自觉遵守，对真正的攻击者毫无约束力，服务端必须自己强制执行。
公共 WiFi、公司网络这类共享 IP 容易被误伤，所以要放松 IP 规则、更依赖已登录用户的限额。
optionExplanations_en: Temporarily blocklisting a client after repeated violations is cheaper than letting it hit the limiter over and over.
Upstream protection like Cloudflare or AWS Shield blocks a layer of traffic before it ever reaches your own Redis, easing pressure on the limiter behind it.
Relying entirely on client good behavior puts zero constraint on an actual attacker — enforcement has to live on the server.
Shared IPs from public WiFi or corporate networks get falsely caught by strict IP rules, so easing those and leaning on authenticated user limits avoids punishing real users.

q: client-side rate limiting 在本设计中的定位是什么？
q_en: What role does client-side rate limiting play in this design?
options: 完全替代服务端限流
只用于数据库内部
有价值的补充，可平滑好公民流量，但不能作为安全边界
会让 HTTP 429 不再需要
why: 客户端限流能减少误伤和基础设施压力，但恶意客户端不会自觉遵守；服务端限流仍是保护系统必须有的边界。
why_en: Client-side limiting is a useful complement for well-behaved clients, but it cannot replace server-side enforcement.
tradeoff: 降低基础设施压力 vs 无法充当安全边界
options_en: A full replacement for server-side rate limiting
Something only used inside the database
A valuable complement that smooths well-behaved traffic, but not a security boundary
Something that makes HTTP 429 unnecessary
optionExplanations: 如果只靠客户端自己限流，恶意或改过的客户端可以直接跳过检查，服务端就完全没有保护了。
限流本来就发生在请求进入系统之前，跟数据库内部操作没有关系，这个选项文不对题。
客户端限流能提前劝退好公民的重试风暴，减轻网络和基础设施压力，但它管不住不听话的客户端，所以服务端限流仍然是唯一硬边界。
客户端主动少发请求不代表服务端就不会再拒绝超限请求，429 该返回还是要返回。
optionExplanations_en: If enforcement lives only on the client, a malicious or modified client can just skip the check, and the server has no protection left.
Rate limiting happens before a request even reaches the system — it has nothing to do with database internals, so this option is off-topic.
Client-side limiting can head off well-behaved clients' retry storms and ease load on the network, but it can't control a client that ignores it, so server-side limiting stays the only real boundary.
Sending fewer requests voluntarily doesn't stop the server from rejecting ones that still go over the limit — 429 still has to fire.

scenario: 限流规则偶尔调整，例如产品发布时临时提高 limit；允许几十秒内逐步生效，想保持实现简单。
scenario_en: Rate-limit rules change occasionally, such as temporarily raising a limit for a product launch; taking tens of seconds to propagate is fine, and the team wants a simple implementation.
q: 最常见的动态配置方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most common approach for dynamic configuration?
options: 每个请求都触发重新部署 gateway
把规则直接写进客户端代码里
只靠人工 SSH 登录改内存
配置库存规则，gateway 定期 polling 并缓存
why: 配置服务/数据库存规则，gateway 周期性 polling 并本地缓存，实现简单、够用；代价是变更到全网生效有延迟，比如最多 30 秒。
why_en: Polling a configuration store and caching results locally is simple and good enough when rule changes can take up to about 30 seconds to propagate.
whenOtherWins: 安全事件或高频交易等需要秒级强推配置时，push-based 方案更合适。
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 变更生效有延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
Admin[Admin config] --> Store[Config store]
Store --> Watch[Watch or poll]
Watch --> Gateway[Gateway cache]
Gateway --> Checks[Limiter checks]
options_en: Redeploy the gateway on every single request
Hard-code the rules directly into client code
Only change memory by hand over SSH
Store rules in a config store; gateways poll and cache them
optionExplanations: 每个请求都触发一次重新部署，部署本身要几十秒到几分钟，这比要改的限额生效速度慢了好几个数量级。
规则写死在客户端代码里，改一次限额要等所有客户端升级完才生效，跟「临时调整」这个诉求正好相反。
靠人工登录改内存，改一台生效一台，规模一大根本没法保证所有 gateway 同步更新。
规则存进配置库，gateway 周期性拉取并本地缓存，实现简单，几十秒内传播完成也在这里能接受的范围内。
optionExplanations_en: Triggering a redeploy on every single request means waiting tens of seconds to minutes for the deploy itself — orders of magnitude slower than the limit needs to take effect.
Hard-coding rules into client code means a limit change only takes effect once every client has been upgraded — the opposite of a quick, temporary adjustment.
Changing memory by hand over SSH updates one gateway at a time, which doesn't scale to keeping every gateway in sync.
Storing rules in a config store that gateways poll and cache locally is simple to build, and propagating within tens of seconds is exactly what this scenario can tolerate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把配置(限流规则)发到各 gateway 的两种方式:poll=每台定期去配置库拉+本地缓存(简单,生效延迟=拉取间隔,如30秒);push=配置变了主动推给各台(实时,但要推送/订阅设施,更复杂)。容忍几十秒→选 poll(更简单),这题正是
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two ways to distribute config (rate-limit rules) to gateways: poll = each gateway periodically fetches from a config store and caches (simple; propagation delay = poll interval, e.g. 30s); push = the store pushes changes (real-time but needs pub/sub infra). If tens of seconds is acceptable, poll is simpler.

termDefinitions.meaning: 安全地远程登录到另一台服务器命令行的协议/工具。你在自己电脑上敲 ssh user@服务器IP,连接被加密,然后就像坐在那台服务器前一样敲命令(看日志、改配置、重启服务)。服务器在机房/云里没接键盘,运维就靠 SSH 进去操作。「人工 SSH 改内存」=工程师手动登进每台机器改 → 不 scale
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSH (Secure Shell) securely logs you into a remote server command line. You run ssh user@host from your laptop; the connection is encrypted and you get a shell on that server (view logs, edit config, restart). Servers sit in data centers with no keyboard, so ops use SSH to operate them. Manually SSH-ing to edit memory means logging into each machine by hand, which does not scale.

scenario: 安全事件中需要几秒内把新 limit 推到所有 gateway，不能等下一轮 30 秒 polling。
scenario_en: During a security incident, a new limit must reach all gateways within seconds — it can't wait for the next 30-second polling cycle.
q: 应考虑哪种配置分发？
q_en: Which configuration-distribution approach should be considered?
options: 用 ZooKeeper/Pub-Sub 做 push 配置通知
每天定时人工重启所有 gateway 才生效
把规则直接写死在部署镜像里
只手动更新其中一台 gateway
why: push-based 配置能立刻通知所有连接的 gateway，适合紧急规则变更；代价是要处理连接故障、部分更新和 fallback，复杂度更高。
why_en: Push-based configuration notifies every connected gateway immediately, which suits urgent changes but adds connection and partial-failure handling complexity.
whenOtherWins: 普通业务规则调整用 polling 更简单；push 只在对传播延迟敏感时才值得付出复杂度。
tradeoff: 秒级生效 vs 连接管理和部分失败的复杂度
options_en: Push-based notification via ZooKeeper or Pub/Sub
Restart every gateway by hand on a daily schedule
Bake the rules directly into the deployment image
Manually update just one single gateway

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式协调服务，能在配置变化时主动推送通知给所有连接的客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service that can push configuration changes to all connected clients immediately.

optionExplanations: ZooKeeper 或 Pub/Sub 能在配置一变就主动推给所有连着的 gateway，秒级生效，正好赶上安全事件的时间要求。
每天定时重启才生效，意味着安全事件发生后最多要等快一整天，跟「几秒内」这个要求差了几个数量级。
规则写进部署镜像意味着改一次限额要重新构建、发布整个镜像，速度上完全跟不上紧急变更。
只手动更新一台 gateway，其余的还在用旧规则，攻击者绕过没更新的那些实例照样能打进来。
optionExplanations_en: ZooKeeper or Pub/Sub can push a config change out to every connected gateway the moment it happens, hitting seconds-level propagation — exactly what a security incident needs.
Restarting on a daily schedule means an incident-time change could wait almost a full day to take effect, off by orders of magnitude from a few seconds.
Baking rules into the deployment image means every limit change needs a full rebuild and rollout — far too slow for an urgent change.
Manually updating just one gateway leaves the rest running old rules, so traffic can still slip through the ones that never got updated.

q: 把“选择 API Gateway + Redis Token Bucket”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing API Gateway plus Redis Token Bucket into the correct order:
steps: 用 Token Bucket 兼顾 burst 和 sustained rate
需求：每个请求前低延迟判断并保护后端
把限流放在 API Gateway，先于业务服务拒绝
用 Redis 共享各 gateway 的 bucket 状态
用 Lua 保证 read-calculate-update 原子
why: 先确定入口保护位置，再选算法，然后补共享状态和原子性；这条链覆盖了功能、延迟和正确性三层。
why_en: The gateway-plus-Redis decision starts with edge protection, chooses Token Bucket, and adds shared atomic state.

q: 把“扩展到 1M RPS”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for scaling to 1M RPS into the correct order:
steps: 每个 shard 做 master-replica 和 failover
用 Redis Cluster / consistent hashing 按 client key 分片
需求：单 Redis 实例只能处理约 50k-100k checks/sec
在 gateway 侧复用连接并尽量区域内访问
约十个 shard 才能达到 1M checks/sec 量级
why: 先由单实例瓶颈推出分片，再估算 shard 数，之后补高可用和低延迟；顺序体现容量、可用性、延迟三层约束。
why_en: Scaling to one million checks requires Redis sharding by client key, enough shards, replica failover, and low-latency connections.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Scale[1M checks per sec] --> Shard[Redis Cluster]
Shard --> Pool[Connection pools]
Pool --> Local[Regional deploy]
Local --> Metrics[Monitor hot keys]

q: 中级候选人在这题里至少应讲清楚什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate clearly cover at minimum in this question?
options: 从零手写一遍完整 ZooKeeper 实现
选对部署位置、讲清一种算法、知道要分片 Redis
背出 Lua 虚拟机的内部源码
只讨论前端错误提示文案
why: 中级重点是高层设计和核心组件理解：放在哪里、怎么算、状态放哪、怎么返回 429；分布式细节可以留到追问再展开。
why_en: A mid-level answer should place the limiter sensibly, explain one algorithm like Token Bucket, and recognize that Redis state needs sharding.
options_en: Implement a full ZooKeeper from scratch
Place the limiter well, explain one algorithm, and know Redis needs sharding
Recite the internal source of the Lua VM
Only discuss frontend error copy
optionExplanations: 从零手写 ZooKeeper 远超中级面试的期望深度，属于过度工程。
选对部署位置、讲清一种算法、知道 Redis 要分片，覆盖了中级候选人该讲清楚的高层设计。
背 Lua 虚拟机内部源码是无关的实现细节，不是系统设计面试考察的内容。
只谈前端错误提示文案完全没碰到这道题真正的技术判断——放哪里、怎么算、状态怎么共享。
optionExplanations_en: Implementing ZooKeeper from scratch goes far beyond what a mid-level interview expects — over-engineering for this scope.
Placing the limiter well, explaining one algorithm clearly, and knowing Redis needs sharding covers the high-level design a mid-level candidate should nail.
Reciting the Lua VM's internal source is an unrelated implementation detail, not what a system-design interview is testing.
Only discussing frontend error copy never touches the actual technical judgment this question is testing — placement, algorithm, shared state.

scenario: 面试官让你设计 1M rps 的 distributed rate limiter。你已经说了 API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket，接下来要体现 senior 深度。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design a distributed rate limiter for 1M rps. You've already said API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket, and now need to show senior-level depth.
q: 下一步最应该主动展开什么？
q_en: What should you proactively expand on next?
options: 只死记硬背固定窗口的定义
假装系统完全没有故障模式
讲清原子更新、按 key 分片、降级
把限流丢给客户端就当结束
why: Senior 深度不是多背算法名，而是说明限流状态在并发、容量和故障下是否仍正确：原子更新、按 key 分片、故障降级。
why_en: Senior depth means explaining whether shared rate-limit state remains correct under concurrency, scale, and Redis failure, not merely naming more algorithms.
options_en: Only recite the definition of a fixed window
Pretend the system has no failure modes
Explain atomic updates, sharding, and failure degradation
Hand rate limiting to the client and stop there

termDefinitions.meaning: 这里指一次限流判断里的“读 token、补 token、扣 token、写回状态”必须像一个不可拆开的步骤执行；否则多个 gateway 并发请求会互相覆盖，导致多放行或误拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Here atomicity means the read-refill-decrement-write rate-limit update runs as one indivisible step, so concurrent gateways cannot overwrite each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同 client 的 bucket 状态分散到多个 Redis shard；同一个 user/IP/API key 必须稳定落到同一个 shard，否则它的计数会被拆散，限流失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding spreads different clients' bucket state across Redis shards while keeping the same client key on the same shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 慢、超时或 shard 挂掉时系统如何反应：fail-open 是放行保可用性但可能打爆后端，fail-closed 是拒绝保护后端但会挡住正常用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A failure mode is how the system behaves when Redis is slow or down, such as fail-open for availability or fail-closed for backend protection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当限流依赖(Redis)故障/超时、判不了限额时,系统「优雅退化」到一个后备行为而不是崩溃。两个主选:fail-open(放行,保可用、失保护)、fail-closed(拒绝,保后端、牺牲可用);更软的还有:退回本地内存近似计数、用上次缓存的规则、临时上一个粗粒度全局限流。所以「降级」=故障时怎么优雅后备,fail-open/close 是它最主要的两个选项
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation: when the rate-limit dependency (Redis) fails/times out and you cannot check limits, the system falls back to a safe behavior instead of crashing. Two main choices: fail-open (allow — keep availability, lose protection) and fail-closed (reject — protect backend, lose availability); softer options include local approximate counting, using last cached rules, or a coarse global cap.

rows: Lua 保证读改写不中断
按 key 分散到多个 shard

optionExplanations: 只讲固定窗口的定义还停留在 junior/mid 的算法背诵，讲不出并发更新同一个 bucket 时会不会出错。
假装系统没有故障模式太危险——分布式限流必须讲清 Redis 超时、shard 挂掉、重试风暴时后端怎么保护。
senior 深度要能讲清三件事：多个 gateway 并发更新会不会踩坏同一份状态、Redis 单点会不会成为新的瓶颈、故障时怎么在保护后端和放行用户之间做取舍。
把限流全丢给客户端只能当补充，攻击者或异常客户端不会可靠配合，服务端还是需要强制手段。
optionExplanations_en: Only reciting the fixed-window definition is still junior/mid-level recall — it doesn't explain whether concurrent gateways can corrupt the same bucket.
Pretending there are no failure modes is risky — a distributed limiter has to explain what happens when Redis times out, a shard dies, or retries spike.

Covering atomic updates, per-key sharding, and failure degradation shows the depth interviewers want, because those are exactly where state gets lost, Redis becomes a single point of failure, or the backend gets overloaded.
Handing everything to the client only works as a complement — attackers or buggy clients won't reliably cooperate, so the server still needs enforcement.

q: Staff+ 答案通常应体现什么？
q_en: What should a Staff+ answer typically demonstrate?
options: 只是多罗列几种算法的名字而已
完全回避任何权衡取舍的讨论
假设所有客户端天生值得信任
强调生产深度：多区域、可观测性、真实容量
why: Staff+ 重点是生产经验和边界条件，能把限流系统放进真实平台运维中思考，而不是更长的术语列表。
why_en: Staff-level answers emphasize production operations, multi-region behavior, observability, and real capacity judgment from experience.
options_en: Just list a few more algorithm names
Avoid any discussion of trade-offs entirely
Assume every client is inherently trustworthy
Emphasize production depth: multi-region, observability, real capacity
optionExplanations: 多报几个算法名字只是知识广度，staff+ 更想听到的是怎么把这套系统在生产里跑稳。
回避权衡取舍恰恰是资历不够的信号——每个方案都有代价，staff+ 应该主动点出来。
假设所有客户端天生可信，等于把安全边界让给了不可控的一方，这在生产系统里是个隐患。
多区域延迟、可观测性、真实容量数字，这些是只有真在生产系统里踩过坑才会主动讲到的深度。
optionExplanations_en: Naming a few more algorithms is just breadth of knowledge — what a staff+ answer needs to show is how the system stays stable in production.
Avoiding tradeoffs is itself a sign of shallower experience — every option has a cost, and a staff+ answer should call it out unprompted.
Assuming every client is inherently trustworthy hands the security boundary over to a party you don't control — a real production risk.
Multi-region latency, observability, and real capacity numbers are exactly the depth that only shows up once you've actually run a system like this in production.

q: 最终 rate limiter 设计的关键组成包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are the key components of the final rate limiter design? (multi-select)
options: API Gateway 执行限流并返回 429 headers
Redis Cluster 分片存 token bucket 状态
Lua 原子执行 bucket 更新
每个请求长期写入分析数据库后再决定是否放行
why: 最终主路径要短：gateway 提取标识、命中对应 Redis shard、脚本原子判断，超限就快速返回 429；长期分析不该阻塞在线决策。
why_en: The final design keeps the hot path short: extract identity, hit the right Redis shard, decide atomically, and return 429 fast when over the limit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> GW[API Gateway]
GW -->|extract id| Router[Shard Router]
Router --> R1[(Redis Shard A)]
Router --> R2[(Redis Shard B)]
Router --> R3[(Redis Shard C)]
R1 --> Rep1[Replica]
GW -->|allow| App[Backend API]
GW -->|429 headers| Client
options_en: The API Gateway enforces limits and returns 429 headers
Redis Cluster shards store token-bucket state
Lua executes bucket updates atomically
Every request is written to an analytics database before deciding
optionExplanations: gateway 执行限流并回传 429 headers，是用户能直接感知到的那一层。
Redis Cluster 按 shard 存 token bucket 状态，把单实例扛不住的量级摊开。
Lua 保证一次 bucket 更新的读改写不被拆开，是并发正确性的关键。
先把每个请求写进分析数据库再决定放不放行，等于把在线判断路径接上一个离线系统的延迟，跟低延迟目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: The gateway enforcing the limit and returning 429 headers is the layer users actually feel.
Redis Cluster sharding token-bucket state spreads out the load a single instance couldn't handle.
Lua keeps a single bucket update's read-modify-write from being split apart, which is what keeps it correct under concurrency.
Writing every request to an analytics database before deciding whether to allow it bolts an offline system's latency onto the online decision path, working against the low-latency goal.
